headline: Back near breakeven as defense and services carry
summary_short: Revenue rose 4% to $24.2B and Boeing posted a GAAP loss of $0.26 per share, versus a $7.14 loss a year ago. Free cash flow was $464M and backlog hit a record $745B.
summary_long: Defense, Space & Security revenue grew 15% to $7.9B, including a $252M gain on the HRL Laboratories sale. Global Services revenue rose 4% with an 18.3% margin. Commercial Airplanes revenue fell 3% to $10.7B with a (6.5)% margin on delivery mix, production-rate costs and supply chain costs, despite 161 deliveries. Operating cash flow was $1.5B after about $0.7B of DOJ settlement payments. Cash was $20.7B against $45.9B debt.
confidence_notes: Year-ago quarter included a 777X program charge, so loss comparisons are not meaningful (NM). Free cash flow and core EPS are non-GAAP measures as defined by Boeing. No financial guidance in the release.

drivers.explanation: Higher defense and services volume, partly offset by less favorable commercial delivery mix.
Prior-year quarter carried a 777X charge; this year Defense earnings benefited from a $252M HRL Laboratories gain while Commercial Airplanes stayed loss-making.
Working capital timing helped, partly offset by roughly $0.7B of Department of Justice settlement payments and higher PP&E spending in Charleston and St. Louis.
CEO points to 737-7 and 737-10 certification and the Navy F/A-XX selection as milestones while stressing safety, quality and Lean execution.
